This catch-up restores two Blue Note Tokyo dates that clear RADAR admission without scarcity inflation: Monday Michiru is A; Ayatake Ezaki with guest Kei Matsumaru is A+.

events.subtitle: Special Summer Live 2026
events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents Monday Michiru's Special Summer Live 2026 on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, with sets at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM. The official venue page announces Monday Michiru on vocals and flute with Jun Miyakawa on piano, Satoshi Yoshida on guitar, Yoshihito 'P' Koizumi on bass, and Tomoaki Kanno on drums. Blue Note frames the one-night session around Michiru's long New York-Tokyo trajectory and her movement among jazz, soul, Latin music, and organic groove.

en.why_it_matters: The reason to keep this on RADAR is the language around the band, not celebrity or nostalgia. Monday Michiru has spent decades connecting Tokyo and New York club-jazz culture, and this one-night lineup gives her flute and voice a rhythm section that can move naturally through jazz, soul, Latin color, and acid-jazz groove without flattening those styles into a revue. It is a strong snapshot of a specific Japanese crossover lineage that the older S-only filter was structurally unable to retain.
en.trip_verdict: Worth keeping on the board if August 25 is open in Tokyo. I would take one of the two sets if the night is free, but I would not move a rarer master, premiere, reunion, or one-off to make room for it.

es.why_it_matters: La razón para mantenerla en el RADAR está en el lenguaje de la banda, no en la fama ni en la nostalgia. Monday Michiru lleva décadas conectando la cultura de club-jazz de Tokio y Nueva York, y esta formación de una sola noche pone su voz y su flauta frente a una sección capaz de moverse con naturalidad entre jazz, soul, color latino y groove de acid jazz sin convertir todo en un popurrí. Es una buena fotografía de una genealogía japonesa de cruce de géneros que el viejo filtro de sólo S/S+ era incapaz de conservar.
es.trip_verdict: Vale tenerla en el tablero si el 25 de agosto está libre en Tokio. Iría a uno de los dos sets si la noche está despejada, pero no desplazaría por esto a un maestro más raro, un estreno, una reunión o una fecha realmente irrepetible.

events.artist: Ayatake Ezaki with guest Kei Matsumaru
events.subtitle: 2026 Japan Tour — Tokyo
events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents Ayatake Ezaki with guest Kei Matsumaru on August 28 and 29, 2026 as the Tokyo stop of Ezaki's 47-prefecture Japan tour. The August 28 sets begin at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM; the August 29 sets begin at 4:30 PM and 7:30 PM. The official page identifies Ezaki on piano and keyboards and Matsumaru on saxophone, with a program expected to draw from Ezaki's 2026 album Whispers of Silence as well as film and television score material. Blue Note specifically notes Ezaki's use of piano, Rhodes, and synthesizers across the project.

en.why_it_matters: This is a strong contemporary-Japan entry because the instruments and current writing are the point. Ezaki moves among acoustic piano, Rhodes and synthesizers, while Matsumaru brings a saxophone language comfortable with both composed space and open improvisation. The Blue Note stop lets the current Whispers of Silence material sit next to Ezaki's screen work instead of forcing him into a single jazz or classical category. That combination is distinctive enough to merit active prioritization even though the larger 47-prefecture tour removes any claim of scarcity.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the four sets if the Tokyo calendar allows it, especially if the trip is already tracing contemporary Japanese instrumental music. The two-night run and nationwide tour give enough flexibility that it should not displace a genuinely rare one-off.

es.why_it_matters: Ésta entra fuerte por Japón contemporáneo porque aquí importan los instrumentos y la escritura actual. Ezaki se mueve entre piano acústico, Rhodes y sintetizadores, mientras Matsumaru trae un lenguaje de saxofón cómodo tanto con el espacio compuesto como con la improvisación abierta. La parada de Blue Note permite que el material de Whispers of Silence conviva con la música que Ezaki ha escrito para cine y televisión, sin obligarlo a caber sólo en jazz o clásica. Esa combinación sí merece prioridad activa, aunque una gira de 47 prefecturas elimina cualquier argumento de escasez.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los cuatro sets si el calendario de Tokio lo permite, sobre todo si el viaje ya viene siguiendo música instrumental japonesa contemporánea. Las dos noches y la gira nacional dan suficiente margen para no desplazar por esto una fecha verdaderamente irrepetible.
